```{=html}
<section class="article-section">
  <div class="container">
    <div class="articles-list">
      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Models Overview</h2>
        <p style="margin-bottom: 2rem; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.8; color: var(--text-dark);">
          This section contains mathematical models and simulations implemented across various platforms 
          for analyzing golf biomechanics, control-affine systems, and multibody dynamics. Each model 
          category provides tools and documentation for understanding the underlying physics and control 
          principles.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Model Categories</h2>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-simulink.html">Matlab Simulink Models</a></h3>
          <p>Control-affine system models, drift-input decomposition simulations, and golf swing dynamics 
          implemented in Matlab Simulink. These models implement the theoretical framework developed in 
          the Drifter Manifesto series, providing numerical simulations and analysis tools. Includes 
          comprehensive documentation of numerical routines, model structure, and supporting technical 
          notes. Visit the <a href="models-simulink.html">Matlab Simulink Models page</a> for detailed 
          documentation and implementation details.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-mujoco.html">MuJoCo Models</a></h3>
          <p>Physics-based simulations using MuJoCo (Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact) for biomechanical 
          analysis, including golf swing models, pendulum systems, and multibody dynamics simulations. 
          MuJoCo provides fast and accurate physics simulation for model-based optimization and analysis. 
          The <a href="models-mujoco.html">MuJoCo Models page</a> includes links to software resources, 
          documentation, and tutorials.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-drake.html">Drake Models</a></h3>
          <p>Robotics and control system models implemented in Drake, focusing on underactuated systems, 
          manipulation, and control-affine dynamics. Drake is an open-source toolbox from MIT's Robot 
          Locomotion Group that provides tools for modeling, simulation, and control of complex robotic 
          systems. The <a href="models-drake.html">Drake Models page</a> includes links to Russ Tedrake's 
          courses, installation guides, and comprehensive support resources.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-pinnochio.html">Pinnochio Models</a></h3>
          <p>Rigid body dynamics and kinematics models using Pinocchio, including forward/inverse dynamics, 
          Jacobian computations, and constraint handling for multibody systems. Pinocchio provides efficient 
          algorithms for robot dynamics and kinematics, based on Roy Featherstone's "Rigid Body Dynamics 
          Algorithms." The <a href="models-pinnochio.html">Pinocchio Models page</a> includes links to 
          Featherstone's website, his classic text, and software resources.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-pendulum.html">Pendulum Models</a></h3>
          <p>Pendulum-based models and simulations that serve as simplified analogs for understanding golf 
          swing dynamics, including single, double, and multi-link pendulum systems. These models provide 
          insights into control-affine systems, drift-input decomposition, and the fundamental physics of 
          underactuated multibody systems. The <a href="models-pendulum.html">Pendulum Models page</a> 
          includes links to related articles and theoretical foundations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-opensim.html">OpenSim Models</a></h3>
          <p>Biomechanics simulation models using OpenSim, a freely available, open-source software platform 
          for modeling, simulating, and analyzing the neuromusculoskeletal system. OpenSim enables building 
          and analyzing musculoskeletal models, performing inverse kinematics and dynamics, and simulating 
          movement. The <a href="models-opensim.html">OpenSim Models page</a> includes links to the OpenSim 
          website, documentation, tutorials, and model repository.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="models-myosim.html">MyoSim Models</a></h3>
          <p>Muscle-driven movement simulation models using MyoSim, an open-source software library for 
          simulating muscle-driven movement. MyoSim provides tools for biomechanical modeling and analysis, 
          enabling researchers to build and simulate models of muscle-tendon systems and analyze muscle 
          activation patterns. The <a href="models-myosim.html">MyoSim Models page</a> includes links 
          to the GitHub repository, documentation, and support resources.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Interactive Tools</h2>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="tools/wrist-universal-joint/grip_angle_simulator.html">Wrist Universal Joint Model</a></h3>
          <p>Interactive application modeling the wrist as a universal joint with proper kinematics. Explore how grip angle and wrist deviation affect torque transmission to the club's shaft axis and high-inertia axis, with real-time visualization and calculations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="content/Wrist as Universal Joint/Universal_Joint_Model_Enhanced.py">Wrist Universal Joint Model (PyQt6)</a></h3>
          <p>Enhanced PyQt6 desktop application with advanced GUI features. Download and run locally for full interactive control over grip angle, wrist angle, club properties, and signal generation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```
